plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional vector field plot drawn inside a light blue wireframe cube, with black x, y, and z axes running through it; x points toward the lower left, y to the right, and z vertically. A small shaded blue sphere sits where the axes cross, marked with the label 0, standing for a large mass at the origin. Arrows fill the interior of the cube and every one points inward toward that sphere. Those closest to the origin are long and bright orange, those at intermediate distance shorter and teal, and those near the corners and faces reduced to small dashes, so length and color together carry the magnitude of the field. Several of the longest arrows lie along the axis directions and meet the sphere head on. Because length and direction vary independently, the reader takes in both at once: the field aims at the central mass everywhere, and its strength climbs sharply as distance to the origin shrinks. The plot renders the gravitational field of a point mass, making visible the uniformly attractive radial direction and the rapid growth in magnitude near the source.

elements: light-blue wireframe cube (12 edges) centered at the origin
black x-axis through the origin pointing toward lower-left with arrowhead and label 'x'
black y-axis through the origin pointing right with arrowhead and label 'y'
black z-axis through the origin pointing vertically up with arrowhead and label 'z'
small shaded blue sphere at the origin representing the central mass
label '0' just below-right of the central sphere
3D lattice of inward-pointing arrows filling the cube interior and faces, all aimed at the origin
arrow length and color encoding field magnitude: long bright-orange near the origin, medium teal at mid-radius, tiny dashes near the cube corners/faces
several longest arrows lying along the +/- axis directions meeting the sphere head-on
one highlighted sample vector (distinct color, e.g. magenta) at a learner-controlled radius used by the distance slider

interactions.teaches: Rotating the cube confirms the field is radial in all three dimensions: from every viewing angle the arrows converge on the single central mass, not just in one plane

interactions.label: Distance r from mass
interactions.teaches: Dragging the highlighted sample point inward makes its arrow lengthen and shift toward orange while it keeps pointing straight at the origin, showing that the gravitational field always aims at the mass and its magnitude grows sharply as 1/r^2 when r shrinks

interactions.label: Field view
interactions.teaches: Switching to equal-length inward arrows isolates the purely attractive radial direction; switching back restores the scaled arrows, making clear that direction (always inward) and strength (inverse-square in distance) are two independent pieces of information the field carries

demo_steps.title: Scaled gravitational field
demo_steps.narration: In the magnitude view the arrows near the blue sphere are long and orange while those near the cube faces shrink to teal dashes — length and color together show the field strengthening toward the mass.

demo_steps.title: Direction only
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to equal-length arrows: every vector still points exactly at the origin, revealing the uniform attractive radial direction once magnitude is factored out.

demo_steps.title: Sample point close to the mass
demo_steps.narration: Back in the scaled view, drag the highlighted sample vector to r=0.6. It becomes much longer and bright orange, demonstrating the steep 1/r^2 rise in field strength near the source.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World space: cube side 4 units centered at origin, edges spanning x,y,z in [-2,2]; draw as LineSegments in light blue #7fb3e6. Axes as black lines from about -3 to +3 with cone arrowheads; +x toward screen lower-left, +y to the right, +z up (standard isometric pose). Central sphere SphereGeometry radius ~0.28, blue radial-gradient #4a90d9 with darker rim, label '0' offset to lower-right. Vector lattice: place sample points on a 5x5x5 grid over [-1.6,1.6]^3, omitting the central cell; at each point draw an arrow pointing toward the origin. Field magnitude m = 1/r^2 (gravitational), capped so the nearest arrows are ~0.7 units long and farthest ~0.06 (a short dash). Color map by normalized magnitude: high -> orange #ff6a00, mid -> teal #1a8a8a, low -> dark teal #14606a. In 'Direction only' mode force every arrow to a fixed length ~0.35 and a single teal color. Highlighted sample vector drawn along the +x direction at radius r (slider), length = clamp(k/r^2), color from the same map but rendered magenta #d0208a with a small sphere at its tail so it reads as the draggable probe. Keep total arrow count <= ~120 for performance; use InstancedMesh or merged LineSegments for shafts plus small cones for heads.
interactionPlan.notes: Build arrows as instanced cylinders+cones oriented via lookAt toward the origin so re-coloring and re-scaling on slider/toggle change is cheap (update instance matrices and colors, do not rebuild geometry). For the toggle, keep two precomputed length/color sets and lerp or swap. Render the sample probe on top with depthTest slightly biased so it stays visible. Add subtle ambient + directional light for the sphere shading; keep cube and axes unlit line material. Label 'x','y','z','0' as screen-space sprites anchored to axis tips and the sphere so they stay legible under orbit.
